name: Artificial Peace
label: Dischord
lede: Four kids from Bethesda built one of the biggest followings in early DC hardcore, cut seventeen songs in one Inner Ear session, got three of them onto Flex Your Head, and were gone before most people heard the rest.

eras.title: Bethesda comes to town
eras.text: Artificial Peace came out of the Maryland suburbs, tight, fast and aggressive, and by Dischord's account drew one of the largest followings of any early DC band. They were also among the first from the area to take the music outside it.

years.h: Artificial Peace forms from Red C and Assault and Battery
years.p: Guitarist [[Pete Murray|6ab4a566-a279-441a-af5f-4d47459e1c18]] comes over from Red C. Singer [[Steve Polcari|33611a9d-0a07-418b-ac27-b51a58f93561]], bassist [[Rob Moss|3ff1431f-c33e-47f4-80ae-df8c0ba0d7fb]] and drummer [[Mike Manos|2da8a8ac-dab6-4b39-9ca6-ce91fee93fcf]] come from Assault and Battery.

years.h: Artificial Peace draw a big crowd and play out of town
years.p: Dischord remembers Artificial Peace as one of the most followed early DC bands, and among the first from the area to play beyond it. They made a point of saying they were from Bethesda.

eras.title: Flex Your Head, and done
eras.text: Flex Your Head made Artificial Peace part of the first document of DC hardcore just as the band was ending. Within a year Steve Polcari, Pete Murray and Mike Manos had started Marginal Man, and Rob Moss was touring with Government Issue.

years.h: Artificial Peace's three songs on Flex Your Head
years.p: "Artificial Peace", "Outside Looking In" and "Wasteland", all from the November 1981 Inner Ear session, on the Dischord No. 7 compilation. Wikipedia says the first 4,000 copies sold out within a week.

years.h: Artificial Peace split 7" with The Exiled
years.p: Released on Fountain of Youth Records, the only vinyl of its own Artificial Peace put out while together.

years.h: Artificial Peace folds; Marginal Man begins
years.p: Steve Polcari, Pete Murray and Mike Manos add [[Kenny Inouye|a2ae807d-953b-496b-ac75-62d55c5f0afc]] and [[Andre Lee|b9484df3-7dce-4c9b-be55-072f26ca9498]] and start [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], one of DC's first two-guitar hardcore bands.
The former Artificial Peace bassist goes on the road with Government Issue that year.

eras.title: The session comes out of the vault
eras.text: Nearly three decades later, Dischord put out the whole November 1981 session, and a live tape from 1982 followed. For a band known by three songs, it was the first full picture.

years.h: Artificial Peace's full 1981 session comes out, 29 years on
years.p: In November 1981 [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] recorded all 17 songs of Artificial Peace's set at Inner Ear; only three came out while the band existed. Dischord released the whole session in 2010 as No. 167.
years.xp:
The session runs from "Suburban Wasteland" and "UXB" to "Spook Surf" and "This Means War". Dischord's notes call Artificial Peace one of the leading bands in the DC hardcore scene at the time. The 2010 LP was mastered at Chicago Mastering Service and pressed on translucent orange vinyl.

One of the three songs released in the band's lifetime was "Outside Looking In". Steve Polcari later used that phrase to explain the name of his next band, [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]].

years.h: Artificial Peace's 1982 Wilson Center tape comes out, 40 years on
years.p: Artificial Peace's June 25, 1982 set at DC's Wilson Center was taped and shelved. Alona's Dream Records released it in 2022 as Live At The Wilson Center | June 25, 1982.
